Thanks again for the time today — helpful call. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment before the technical POC.

Highlights from the call:
- Objective: integrate Redwood inference for real-time transaction classification + embeddings-based risk scoring.
- Primary constraints: PCI-adjacent environment, short latency (sub-150ms target on 512-token sequences), strict audit/audit-logs requirement.
- Preferred flows discussed: server-side API via Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with SDK bootstrap on backend services, and optional client-side read-only embed requests from a restricted service account.

Auth options we discussed (recommended path in bold):
1) API keys (long-lived): simplest for initial POC but poor rotation/audit properties — would require gateway for short-lived tokens.
2) OAuth/JWT (short-lived): best for long-term security; Redwood supports JWT service assertions and OIDC flows.
3) Service accounts with short-lived tokens + KMS/HSM integration: recommended for production given your audit/KMS needs.

Recommended immediate approach:
- POC phase (30 days): use short-lived JWT assertions minted by a Ledgerly service account (rotation every 24 hours) backed by your KMS. This gives us least friction for server-side SDK calls and keeps keys off dev machines.
- SDK onboarding: we will share a backend SDK quickstart (Node + Python) that supports automatic token refresh and built-in retry/batching.
- Routing & fallbacks: route low-latency inference to Dedicated in us-west, with automatic fallback to hosted variants for non-sensitive batch reranks.
- Embeddings/reranker: keep embeddings generation server-side, persist keys in your vault, and use response signatures + request IDs for traceability.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Redwood (rafael): produce SDK quickstart, token minting snippet, and a one-page credentialing checklist — ETA 2026-05-20. (attached: ledgerly-integration-diagram.png)
- Ledgerly (Sam): confirm KMS vendor (AWS KMS vs Vault) and whether you can issue a service account with a 24-hr short-lived TTL — ETA 2026-05-19.
- Redwood (marissa): prepare cred-matrix-v1.xlsx with required permissions and evidence for SOC-like review — ETA 2026-05-21.
- Sales (ben): prepare initial POC SOW and targeted cost estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted — ETA 2026-05-22.

Notes on evidence & audit log needs: we flagged the need for per-request metadata retention (user id, request id, model version). Redwood can provide a filtered audit export (S3) for Dedicated customers; we'll include sample export schema in the checklist.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the SDK snippets and the credentialing checklist by Wednesday.
